note: Independent re-quantisation of the pinned bf16 head (EigenLabs/Qwen3.8-27B-MTP-bf16 @ 26a328e070875b0314d652a039b6b59902690f03) to 4-bit affine group-32 with MLX mx.quantize(group_size=32, bits=4), keeping the exact uint32-packed geometry of the shipped 4-bit g64 head (w [out, in/8] uint32 + bf16 scales/biases; 31 tensors) so the scales-keyed loader walk needs no code change. Finer groups (64 -> 32) fit each scale to half the values, moving the approximation between 4-bit g64 (measured acceptance 0.956 vs bf16 0.991) and bf16 at a scale-traffic cost of ~3% of head bytes (the head is ~6-7% of a candidate round). The head only proposes; the pinned target re-verifies every emitted token. sha256 is the tree digest over the single fetched model.safetensors per the documented rule; bytes is the fetched file size. Loadcheck on the M4 rig: all 31 tensors load through MLX's affine loader and dequantize at group 32; worst max-abs error vs bf16 = 0.086 (4-bit step-bounded; o_proj). Prior 8-bit g64 arm (b58565d, eb9ecd7c) failed ranked validation twice; this arm deliberately reuses the PROVEN g64 packing (same loader contract) with only the group size changed.
